extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory, especially those familiar with Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmuller theory and the abc/Vojta conjectures
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and technical development of the ingredients needed to prove the abc-conjecture via arithmetic Teichmuller spaces, including constructions of arithmeticoids/holomorphoids, global Frobenius/log-Links, theta-value loci, and the requisite volume/height bounds leading to Vojta's inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of distinct Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must demonstrate the existence of (distinct) arithmetic holomorphic structures (holomorphoids / arithmeticoids) rather than merely assert them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses the disambiguation problem in Mochizuki's work; Joshi asserts and references results ([Joshi, 2022], [Joshi, 2023a], [Joshi, 2024c]) that provide a metrisable topological space of arithmeticoids and a space of holomorphoids, showing distinct structures exist and can be parameterized (cf. Table 1.9.1 and §1.7 discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-triviality of the valuation-scaling property of Θgau-Link
rubrics_metrics.description: One must establish the existence and non-trivial valuation-scaling property for Mochizuki's Θgau-Link (i.e. that it is not identically trivial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi provides local geometric constructions (via Fargues-Fontaine curves) that realize Θgau-Links and demonstrates their non-trivial valuation-scaling property ([Joshi, 2023b]). This counters the Scholze–Stix objection that such links cannot be non-trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and effect of the log-Link (global Frobenius proxy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-Link (or global Frobenius proxy) must be shown to genuinely modify local and global height functions and be central to the proof strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper explains how applying global Frobenius ϕ changes local non-archimedean contributions to heights hy(x) (see discussion around (2) and references to [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem 10.20.1]), and why log-Links are important in Mochizuki's method (cf. remarks about iterates and log-Link stability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation of the product formula hyperplane (period morphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be genuine variation in the hyperplane given by the global product formula across arithmeticoids, yielding a non-trivial period morphism depending on y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi constructs a period morphism YL → P(⊕v Rv) sending y to Hy, showing the product formula produces a y-dependent hyperplane (see point (5) and references [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem 5.10.1], [Joshi, 2024c, Theorem 4.6.1]). This addresses objections that the product formula hyperplane cannot vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of ΘMochizuki under iterates of global Frobenius
rubrics_metrics.description: The theta-value locus ΘMochizuki (and related sets) should be stable under iterates of the global Frobenius morphism ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability under ϕn is a key property used to control heights and volumes; Joshi constructs ΘMochizuki and shows its stability (cf. discussion in §1.5 and references to [Joshi, 2024c, §9] and [Joshi, 2023b,a]). This stability corresponds to Mochizuki's stability under iterates of log-Link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper and lower bounds on log-volumes of Θ-sets
rubrics_metrics.description: One must obtain explicit lower and upper bounds on log Vol(ΘMochizuki) (or analogous volumes), e.g. inequalities of the form 0 < A ≤ log Vol(Θ_ϕ(y0)) = log Vol(Θ_y0) ≤ A'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof strategy relies on producing such bounds (see equations (1.5.1)–(1.5.6) and Theorem 6.10.1), summing local contributions, and then using a global relation A' = C·A (with C ≥ 1) to deduce Vojta's inequality (Theorem 7.1.1). The paper explains log-shifting / Frobenius-shifting techniques to obtain these comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to compute global log-volumes by summing local contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Log-volumes of adelic/adelic-like sets (Θ-sets) must be decomposable into a sum of local contributions at primes, with controllable nonzero terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi emphasizes that Θ-sets are adelic and most primes contribute zero to the log-volume, so log Vol(Θ) can be computed as ∑_p log Vol_p(Θ_p) (see discussion after (1.5.1)). Mochizuki's upper bound in Theorem 6.10.1 is obtained by summing local contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a global Frobenius morphism and geometric log-Link realizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A global Frobenius morphism (ϕ) and geometric realizations of log-Links (local and global) must be constructed, e.g. via Fargues–Fontaine curves, and shown to have the required properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi constructs global Frobenius and shows that the Frobenius morphism on suitable Fargues–Fontaine curves has the properties of Mochizuki's (local) log-Link ([Joshi, 2023b], [Joshi, 2023a], [Joshi, 2024c]). Worked examples are promised (e.g. [Joshi, 2025a]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability of heights hy(x) and h_{ϕ(y)}(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must explain and control how heights hy(x) change under application of global Frobenius ϕ, including local non-archimedean contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key point: contributions of a non-archimedean prime v to hy(x) change under ϕ (see (2) and [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem 10.20.1]); in elliptic curve contexts, absolute values of Tate parameters rise under ϕ, which motivates log-Link and its iterates. These comparisons are used to bound heights appearing in abc-related estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of Tate divisor by stable divisor q and bounds for q
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Tate(C/M) and Tate2(C/M) may not be stable under field extensions, the argument requires replacing them by a divisor q(C/M) that is stable under base-field extensions and proving key bounds for q (e.g. Theorem 6.1.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi introduces q (supported on primes lying over primes of semi-stable reduction in Lmod) and proves its stability under extensions (Proposition 4.4.4) and key bounds (Theorem 6.1.1, corresponding to [Mochizuki, 2021d, Theorem 1.10]). These bounds are essential in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Initial Θ-Data and ability to work on compactly bounded subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: One must produce Initial Θ-Data on fixed compactly bounded subsets Z ⊂ Ud to construct Θ-sets and reduce the global problem to bounding volumes on these subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Existence of Initial Θ-Data (Theorem 5.7.1) is invoked to talk about ΘMochizuki on a fixed compactly bounded set Z, enabling both lower bound (Corollary 9.11.1.1) and upper bound arguments for volumes (see §1.5 discussion). The reduction to Vojta's inequality applies to compactly bounded subsets of Ud (see §5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration/quantification of Mochizuki's Three Fundamental Indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a canonical geometric description and quantitative account of Ind1, Ind2, Ind3 (Mochizuki's three indeterminacies), especially Ind3 which is the subtlest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi claims to quantify these indeterminacies and to give geometric origin and relationship to arithmetic (see point 5 in §1.6 and references to [Joshi, 2024c, §8.11]). Accurate handling of these indeterminacies is central to making Mochizuki's constructions rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of archimedean contributions in arithmetic holomorphic structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic holomorphic structures (and associated Teichmuller-like theories) must include archimedean contributions and not be purely non-archimedean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi emphasizes that his theory ([Joshi, 2023a]) includes archimedean contributions (point (a) in §1.6(4)), and that these are important for global constructions such as the period morphism and product formula hyperplanes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic construction and naturality of the adelic log-shell
rubrics_metrics.description: One must provide an intrinsic construction of Mochizuki's adelic log-shell and explain why the log-shell is a natural/ canonical object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi claims to give an intrinsic construction of the adelic log-shell in [Joshi, 2024c], which clarifies its role and naturality in the theory (point (d) in §1.6(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to compare theta-values arising from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures in a common ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta-values from different arithmetic holomorphic structures should be comparable in a fixed adelic period ring BL' (so that multiplicative operations and tensor products are natural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi constructs a ring BL' (product of certain Fargues–Fontaine rings) in which absolute values of Tate parameters arising from distinct structures can be compared, providing an explanation for tensor products appearing in Mochizuki's work and the relationship between Θ_Joshi and Θ_Mochizuki (point (6) in §1.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Frobenius-shifting (log-shifting) to compare volumes and slopes
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof should use Frobenius-shifting (aka log-shifting) techniques—comparing arithmeticoids y0 and ϕ(y0) and using vector-bundle slope comparisons—to relate lower and upper bounds on volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi follows Mochizuki's strategy of using y0 and y'0 = ϕ(y0) (log-shifting) and interpreting the comparison in terms of slopes of filtered vector bundles (see remarks following (1.5.1) and references to [Joshi and Pauly, 2015] and Mochizuki's remarks). This produces inequalities of the form in (1.5.6) used in Theorem 6.10.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to Vojta's Height Inequality on compactly bounded subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: The global abc proof relies on reducing to proving Vojta's Height Inequality for compactly bounded subsets of Ud (via Mochizuki's reduction [Mochizuki, 2010]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi states that Mochizuki's reduction reduces the abc proof to establishing Vojta's Height Inequality (see §7 for statement) on compactly bounded subsets of Ud (see §5.1). The subsequent volume/height bounds yield Vojta's inequality (Theorem 7.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit control of local contributions at finitely many primes
rubrics_metrics.description: In the log-volume comparisons, one must pick real numbers z_p, z'_p (nonzero for only finitely many primes) satisfying global equalities so that the sum of local log-volumes matches the desired global bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper explains (1.5.4)–(1.5.6): choose z_p, z'_p ≥ 0 with only finitely many non-zero to realize A and A' as sums of local log-volumes. This explicit local control is required because local data for y0 and y'0 differ by Frobenius and cannot be compared term-by-term without careful normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent quantification of p-adic Hodge-theoretic aspects (Hodge-Theaters / Hodge structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of p-adic Hodge Theory and collections of Hodge-Theaters must be quantified to make the variation-of-Hodge-structure intuition rigorous and usable in estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi claims to make the role of p-adic Hodge Theory transparent (point (h) in §1.6(4)), providing quantification that was missing in Mochizuki's exposition, thereby allowing Hodge-Theaters to serve concretely as proxies for variations of Hodge structures in estimates.
